_law: The reusable segment library. Formats reference blocks by id and order them via base_sequence + branches. Each block declares its own claim_mode (its truth-contract labels) and evidence, so the same block carries its honesty label into any format. eligible_roles = any ONE of these role types (FORMAT_SYSTEM vocab H/M/A/B/E/W/S/C/P) MAY lead/perform this block. requires = role types that must ALL be present for the block to run (each satisfied by >=1 filled slot of that role); a block with no `requires` is a single-performer block bound to one eligible_roles slot. A partner that is guaranteed by the branch condition that inserts the block (e.g. 'slot cameo filled') need not be listed in requires. CITE-OR-CUT: any block whose claim_mode contains FACT or ATTRIBUTED_CLAIM MUST list at least one evidence device. escalation is 0-5 (0=setup, 5=peak). fallback = what to do when the block's people/assets are missing. entry_cue and exit_condition are derived by the SHOWPLAN compiler from surrounding blocks, not stored per-block.

blocks.name: HEADLINE
blocks.purpose: open on the day's sharpest item as a joke or hook
blocks.fallback: read the item straight

blocks.name: FACT SETUP
blocks.purpose: establish the verified facts of the dispute before anyone argues
blocks.output: shared factual floor + the binary question
blocks.fallback: state what is confirmed and flag what is not

blocks.name: OPENING ARGUMENT
blocks.purpose: one side's uninterrupted case, receipts in hand
blocks.fallback: if only one advocate exists, the branch swaps this for strongest-counterargument

blocks.name: REBUTTAL
blocks.purpose: direct answer to the prior case
blocks.fallback: host voices the rebuttal

blocks.name: CROSSFIRE
blocks.purpose: open collision, interruptions live, moderator referees
blocks.fallback: removed when there is no live B (see moderated-collision branch)

blocks.name: EVIDENCE TEST
blocks.purpose: put a concrete piece of proof against both positions
blocks.fallback: read the strongest available data point aloud

blocks.name: HARDER HYPOTHETICAL
blocks.purpose: moderator raises the stakes from judgment to consequence
blocks.fallback: skip under short runtime

blocks.name: FINAL RESPONSE
blocks.purpose: each side's closing beat
blocks.fallback: one side closes, host notes the empty seat

blocks.name: SCORECARD
blocks.purpose: moderator's one-line ruling on the card - always names a winner or the dominant argument
blocks.output: a verdict: the winner or the single dominant argument
blocks.fallback: name the dominant argument - never leave it a draw or an 'unresolved fault line'

blocks.name: OPENING CLUE
blocks.purpose: start on something that looks unrelated
blocks.output: a question the audience wants answered
blocks.fallback: open on the oldest verifiable artifact

blocks.name: TIMELINE
blocks.purpose: lay out the original sequence of events
blocks.fallback: narrate the two anchor dates only

blocks.name: DOCUMENT REVEAL
blocks.purpose: read the receipt on air
blocks.fallback: quote the on-record statement

blocks.name: CONTRADICTION
blocks.purpose: surface the clash between what was said and what was done
blocks.fallback: state both quotes side by side

blocks.name: THESIS CONNECT
blocks.purpose: connect the contradiction to the current event
blocks.fallback: state the thesis and flag its uncertainty

blocks.name: EXPERT INTERVIEW
blocks.purpose: expert/witness confirms, adds firsthand knowledge, or explains consequences
blocks.fallback: OPTIONAL_PROOF: replace with a taped statement or an extra document-reveal (the E/W partner is guaranteed by the branch that inserts this)

blocks.name: CONSEQUENCES
blocks.purpose: explain what follows and what is still unknown (uncertainty flagged on the claim, not as a label)
blocks.fallback: name the single biggest open question

blocks.name: CLIP REACTION
blocks.purpose: play the defining clip and react
blocks.fallback: describe the clip and quote it

blocks.name: CLIP MONTAGE
blocks.purpose: prove reality is already more absurd than the joke
blocks.fallback: two clips instead of a montage

blocks.name: CORRESPONDENT EXCHANGE
blocks.purpose: a foil takes the target's logic to an absurd extreme
blocks.output: comedic escalation + a real point underneath
blocks.fallback: clip-montage + host commentary

blocks.name: COMEDY BIT
blocks.purpose: a self-contained joke unit
blocks.fallback: cut for time

blocks.name: SUBJECT INTERVIEW
blocks.purpose: interview the principal or subject
blocks.fallback: OPTIONAL_MODULE: drop and run more desk material

blocks.name: CALLBACK CLOSE
blocks.purpose: return to the cold-open joke after the real point lands
blocks.fallback: restate the thesis plainly

blocks.name: CURRENT HOOK
blocks.purpose: brief news material, then pivot into the deep dive
blocks.fallback: open on the single starkest stat

blocks.name: DEFINE PROBLEM
blocks.purpose: state the system-level problem plainly
blocks.fallback: one sentence + one number

blocks.name: MECHANICS
blocks.purpose: explain how the system actually works
blocks.fallback: one worked example

blocks.name: WHO IS AFFECTED
blocks.purpose: show the human cost
blocks.fallback: merge into who-benefits

blocks.name: WHO BENEFITS
blocks.purpose: name accountable actors and their incentives
blocks.fallback: name the single biggest beneficiary

blocks.name: FAILED SOLUTIONS
blocks.purpose: show why prior fixes did not work
blocks.fallback: cut under short runtime

blocks.name: REFORMS
blocks.purpose: present stronger fixes or an audience action
blocks.fallback: one concrete ask

blocks.name: SPECTACLE
blocks.purpose: a memorable visual/comedic capstone
blocks.fallback: a strong closing line

blocks.name: RULES INTRO
blocks.purpose: introduce the subject, the rules, the progression, the final challenge
blocks.output: the format contract with the audience
blocks.fallback: shorten to name + stakes

blocks.name: ROUND
blocks.purpose: one challenge level paired with one escalating question
blocks.fallback: fewer rounds, keep the easy->consequential->final arc

blocks.name: FINAL CHALLENGE
blocks.purpose: hardest challenge + the direct answer to the hardest question
blocks.fallback: the single hardest question, asked plainly

blocks.name: MONOLOGUE
blocks.purpose: host reacts to the week
blocks.fallback: three jokes on the top story

blocks.name: ONE ON ONE
blocks.purpose: host interrogates one major voice
blocks.fallback: MULTI_MODULE: skip, open the panel earlier (the S/E partner is guaranteed by the principal slot)

blocks.name: PANEL COLLISION
blocks.purpose: panelists stress-test the issue against each other
blocks.fallback: run as a pair

blocks.name: FINAL PANEL CONFLICT
blocks.purpose: the sharpest disagreement, unresolved
blocks.fallback: host names the disagreement

blocks.name: CLOSING EDITORIAL
blocks.purpose: host synthesizes or rejects the discussion
blocks.fallback: one committed sentence

blocks.name: COLD OPEN
blocks.purpose: hottest take commits in two sentences; show ID in one breath
blocks.fallback: state the take, name the show

blocks.name: THE FLOOR
blocks.purpose: the lead topic argued; stances locked, receipts flowing
blocks.fallback: two-hander with tighter turns

blocks.name: THE RECEIPT
blocks.purpose: withheld evidence lands live
blocks.fallback: read the receipt plainly - never fabricate one

blocks.name: THE VERDICT
blocks.purpose: the weight-drop reframe + ruling
blocks.fallback: state the ruling in one line

blocks.name: THE BUTTON
blocks.purpose: prediction + comment challenge + tomorrow tease
blocks.fallback: prediction + one comment prompt

blocks.name: THESIS PLANT
blocks.purpose: the take, committed, no wind-up
blocks.fallback: one committed sentence

blocks.name: EVIDENCE RUN
blocks.purpose: receipts delivered like punchlines in service of the thesis
blocks.fallback: the three strongest receipts only

blocks.name: COUNTERPUNCH
blocks.purpose: steelman the strongest objection, then break it
blocks.fallback: name the objection, answer it

blocks.name: FLAG PLANT
blocks.purpose: restate the thesis harder + the dare
blocks.fallback: restate + dare

blocks.name: WIRE OPEN
blocks.purpose: what the wire is carrying today, rapid-fire list
blocks.fallback: name the top three

blocks.name: RAPID FIRE
blocks.purpose: N fast items, hardest first, no item over 60s
blocks.fallback: fewer items, keep hardest first

blocks.name: THE CALLER
blocks.purpose: a distinct call-in outsider character with one unhinged take
blocks.fallback: OPTIONAL_MODULE: drop, add a wire item

blocks.name: WIRE CLOSE
blocks.purpose: the one thing to watch + out
blocks.output: the out on the dial tone
blocks.fallback: name the one thing

blocks.name: STRONGEST COUNTERARGUMENT
blocks.purpose: fill an empty debate seat honestly: the host/moderator states the strongest opposing case
blocks.input: the position with no live advocate
blocks.output: a fair, strong opposing case for the live side to answer
blocks.fallback: state the single strongest objection in one paragraph - never strawman it

blocks.name: REPORTING BLOCK
blocks.purpose: extra sourced reporting when no witness/expert is available
blocks.fallback: one sourced update read on air

blocks.name: DESK STORY
blocks.purpose: a second desk story that replaces a dropped interview module
blocks.fallback: shorten to a single headline + reaction

blocks.name: UPDATED ASSESSMENT
blocks.purpose: replaces the payoff when breaking news changes the premise mid-episode
blocks.output: a re-stated ruling in light of the new facts
blocks.fallback: state what changed and re-rule in one line

blocks.name: A-BLOCK
blocks.purpose: the night's lead as a built case: context -> receipts -> the turn
blocks.output: the built lead, one step short of its conclusion
blocks.fallback: the lead in three receipt beats

blocks.name: B-BLOCK
blocks.purpose: second story or the lead's consequence thread
blocks.fallback: one-line callback + the second story's core

blocks.name: C-BLOCK
blocks.purpose: the lighter item: culture, a birthday, a follow-up watch
blocks.fallback: cut for time

blocks.name: THE LAST WORD
blocks.purpose: anchor's verdict + what to watch tomorrow
blocks.output: a committed verdict + the tomorrow watch
blocks.fallback: one-line verdict
